propositions.claim: A GPO slip printing of EO 6604, dated February 16, 1934 and signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, is held.
propositions.quote: FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT. Tue Waite Houss, February 16, 1934. [No. 6604] U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1934

propositions.claim: The order's one command is a temporary withdrawal of public lands in the listed townships for soil classification.
propositions.quote: all public lands in the townships hereinafter described be, and they are hereby, temporarily withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry, and all forms of appropriation, for the purpose of soil classification

propositions.claim: The withdrawal was made under the Pickett Act as amended, subject to its conditions and valid existing rights; the order has no expiry term of its own.
propositions.quote: By virtue of the authority vested in me by the act of June 25, 1910 (ch. 421, 36 Stat. 847), as amended by the act of August 24, 1912

propositions.claim: A second GPO printing (bound slip-order volume, HathiTrust hvd.hl2725) carries the same operative words.
propositions.quote: temporarily withdrawn from settlement , location , sale , entry , and all forms ofappropriation , for the purpose of soil classification

review.conclusion_reason: NO, formal revocation, and a first ending on April 10, 1951 are asserted despite an acknowledged gap in the revoking instrument. The table's signature date does not establish the operative ending date. The supported assessment is OPEN pending PLO 711's actual revocation language, scope, and effective terms at 16 FR 3348; formal revocation likewise remains unconfirmed. T2 is the highest tier of the submitted result whose required propositions are upheld.

verdicts.reason: The held mabillon text contains Roosevelt's signature, February 16, 1934, [No. 6604], and U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1934.
The held original contains the quoted withdrawal command and the township list; no additional operative command appears.
The full original cites both acts and expressly says 'subject to the conditions therein expressed and to all valid existing rights.' No expiry date or terminating event is specified in its text.

The photius file identifies the GPO bound volume and HathiTrust identifier and reproduces the same withdrawal language. Its preceding unrelated order and truncated signature do not obscure that command.

The held table confirms the quoted entry, signature date, and 16 FR 3348 citation. However, it is a finding aid: the actual PLO 711 revoking sentence, scope, and effective terms were not supplied. The substantive ending claim cannot be upheld from this entry alone under the project rules.
